operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names (Staff, Customers, Products, Complaints) and mixed-case columns; must double-quote with original spelling.
Complaints has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there, and drop_unique_duplicates has nothing to drop.
Complaints.complaint_id is INTEGER NOT NULL but not PK and not unique-declared; distinct=12 on 12 rows, so it looks like a key but TS will not treat it as one.
Products.parent_product_id is a self-referencing-looking integer (values 3,4,8,9) but there is NO declared FK; TS treats it as a plain Number column, not a self-FK.
DATETIME columns store text like '1988-09-29 17:54:50' (space-separated, no T, no timezone); Date fuzzer template must match this format.

DATETIME declared type dispatches to 'Date|Number(int elements)' — first element '1988-09-29 17:54:50' does not parse as int, so Date fuzzer is chosen; but if a pool literal is an int the dispatch could flip to Number(scale=4).
product_price DECIMAL(19,4) has mixed storage classes (real and integer: '35' stored as integer); Number fuzzer with scale=19, precision=4 gives a huge range [-10^19,10^19].
VARCHAR(1) gender stores '0'/'1' (text), not 'M'/'F'; String fuzzer will produce arbitrary 1-char strings.
complaint_outcome_code has distinct=1 ('OK') — a constant column; TS String fuzzer will still emit random strings, breaking any '= OK' filter.
All FK parents exist and are unique PKs (Customers.customer_id, Products.product_id, Staff.staff_id); no dangling FKs, no composite keys.
Tiny tables (Staff 7, Customers 8, Products 4, Complaints 12) — choose_table_sizes will inflate them to 30..2500 rows, so FK fan-out and join cardinalities change drastically.
Complaints.staff_id distinct=6 but Staff has 7 rows — one staff member has no complaints; FK fill with replacement will not preserve this.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on the four DATETIME columns: template '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' (first parsable element), range from min/max of 5 sampled originals, fresh draws uniform in that range; p=0.2 means 20% element reuse.

String fuzzer on all VARCHAR columns: random strings over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' of length in [min,max+1] of sampled originals, with 50% contamination (suffix/prefix/drop-char) — emails, phones, state names become garbage.
Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: fresh uniform in [-10^0,10^0] perturbed by ±1/±2, so staff_id/customer_id/product_id become small ints that may collide with FK draws only by luck.
Number fuzzer on product_price DECIMAL(19,4): scale=19 gives range ±10^19, so prices become astronomically large or negative — implausible values drive FN on price filters.
FK columns (Complaints.product_id/customer_id/staff_id) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement, so referential integrity holds but distribution is uniform over surviving parents.
complaint_outcome_code constant 'OK' in original: TS String fuzzer emits random strings, so any gold query filtering '= OK' returns empty on generated units — likely FN source.
complaint_status_code (Closed/New/Open) and complaint_type_code (Product Failure/Product Unusable) are small enums; TS String fuzzer ignores them, producing values no gold query matches — FN source.
No PK on Complaints: TS will not dedupe rows, so duplicate complaint_id values appear; gold queries with COUNT(DISTINCT complaint_id) vs COUNT(*) diverge — FP/FN source.
Tiny original tables inflated to 30..2500 rows: joins that returned 1-2 rows in original return hundreds; aggregate gold answers (AVG price, COUNT complaints) shift — expected, not a bug.

Date columns have no ordering constraint (closed before raised possible); TS Date fuzzer draws independently per column, so date_complaint_closed < date_complaint_raised frequently — implausible, FN on date-range queries.

parent_product_id values (3,4,8,9) do not match any product_id (117-120) in original — it is not a real FK; TS Number fuzzer will produce values that may accidentally match product_id, creating spurious self-joins.
